skill.name: javascript-sdk
skill.description: Guides JavaScript and TypeScript developers through inference.sh SDK setup, app execution, streaming, file handling, agent tools, and frontend proxy patterns.
skill.summary: Build inference.sh JavaScript and TypeScript SDK integrations for apps, agents, files, streaming, and frontend proxies.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily SDK documentation, and most static matches are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholders, or safe server-side configuration. Real risks remain in two tool-handler examples that use eval() on model or user controlled tool arguments, plus one frontend example that exposes an API key through NEXT_PUBLIC_INFERENCE_API_KEY.

remediation.issue: Tool handler examples use eval() on call.args.expression.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval() with a constrained math parser, a fixed operation map, or a sandboxed calculator service with strict input validation.

remediation.issue: A frontend testing example references NEXT_PUBLIC_INFERENCE_API_KEY as an API key source.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the public key example and direct all browser usage through the documented server proxy, including development setup.

remediation.issue: Powerful agent capabilities are shown with webhooks, file operations, and code execution.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings to require least privilege, user approval, scoped secrets, and audit logging before enabling these capabilities.

content.value_statement: JavaScript teams need clear patterns for AI app execution, agents, files, streaming, and frontend security. This skill provides practical inference.sh SDK guidance for Node.js, TypeScript, React, and server proxies.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install and initialize @inferencesh/sdk in JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
Explains app execution with waiting, fire-and-forget tasks, sessions, and streaming updates.
Documents file upload, download, browser File objects, buffers, streams, and attachments.
Covers agent creation with template agents, ad-hoc agents, tools, approvals, and chat history.
Provides frontend proxy patterns for Next.js, Express, Hono, Remix, and SvelteKit.
Includes TypeScript typing patterns for clients, tasks, tools, errors, and status handling.
limitations: It is documentation guidance, not a runnable SDK package or generated project scaffold.
Examples require a valid inference.sh account, API key, and installed @inferencesh/sdk package.
Some advanced patterns need backend authentication, secret storage, and rate limiting decisions.
Security-sensitive examples should be reviewed before copying into production code.

use_cases.title: Add AI Apps to Node.js Services
use_cases.description: Use the SDK to run inference.sh apps, manage task status, stream progress, and handle errors in a server application.

use_cases.title: Build Secure React AI Features
use_cases.description: Configure browser clients through a backend proxy so React and Next.js apps can call inference.sh without exposing API keys.

use_cases.title: Create Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Combine template agents, custom tools, file attachments, sessions, and human approval for controlled agent experiences.

prompt_templates.title: Install the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add @inferencesh/sdk to my Node.js project and initialize a client with a server-side API key.

prompt_templates.title: Run an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to run an inference.sh app from TypeScript, wait for completion, and handle success or failure.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Frontend Proxy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Next.js proxy route for inference.sh so my React client never receives the API key.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build an inference.sh agent workflow with typed tools, file attachments, streaming responses, and human approval gates.

output_examples.input: Create a secure Next.js setup for browser calls to inference.sh.
output_examples.output: A backend proxy plan with server-side key storage, client proxy configuration, authentication checks, rate limiting, and deployment notes.

output_examples.input: Explain how to stream progress from a long-running image generation task.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step integration outline covering stream options, progress handling, log display, partial output handling, and completion states.

output_examples.input: Review my agent tool design for production readiness.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering tool schemas, approval requirements, secret scope, error handling, audit logs, and safe fallback behavior.

best_practices: Keep inference.sh API keys on trusted servers or secret managers, never in browser bundles.
Use TypeScript types for task status, tool arguments, and error handling to reduce integration mistakes.
Require approval and audit logging for tools that write files, call webhooks, or execute code.
anti_patterns: Do not expose production API keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables or client-side configuration.
Do not evaluate model-generated tool arguments with eval() or other unrestricted code execution.
Do not enable broad webhooks, file access, or code execution without scoped permissions and user confirmation.

faq.question: What package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers the @inferencesh/sdk package for JavaScript and TypeScript projects.

faq.question: Can I use it with React or Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes browser client patterns and server proxy examples for secure frontend integration.

faq.question: Does it support streaming?
faq.answer: Yes. The references explain streaming task progress, logs, partial outputs, and agent message callbacks.

faq.question: Does it handle files?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents uploads, downloads, buffers, streams, browser File objects, and agent file attachments.

faq.question: Is this a full application template?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill with implementation patterns that you adapt inside your own project.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review API key storage, proxy authentication, rate limits, webhook permissions, file access, and tool approval flows.
